newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares rebound, end firm on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares rebound, end firm on short-covering.

text.p: Boosted by Telebras shares and options, Brazilian stocks ended firm on Tuesday, after a weak early session, on short-covering and some buy orders from institutional investors, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares rose 1.16 percent or 749 points, closing at 65,218 points.
Market turnover was still moderate, totalling 349.6 million reais ($342.3 million), but analysts noted activity improved late in the day.
"The market was moving sideways until mid-afternoon, but the mood changed as buying pressure increased," said a trader.
Some analysts attributed today's better-than-expected market behaviour to speculative trades ahead of October's options and futures settlements.
The options are due to be settled on Oct 21, while the futures contracts will be liquidated on Oct 16, traders said.
Considering today's close, the market could continue firming tomorrow, analysts said.
But Thursday's first round of municipal elections could help to keep investors away from the bourses, they noted.
Telebras preferred gained 1.37 percent to close at 81.40 reais, while its common shares rose 1.63 percent, ending at 67.48 reais.
Among other blue-chips, state power utility Eletrobras
Mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) preferred rose 0.25 percent, ending at 20.30 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred ended at 120.99 reais, up 0.83 percent.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the sector rose 2.01 percent, ending at 1,651 points.
